blogs.title: Why Angles Matter: The Science Behind Orthogonal Finetuning for Diffusion Models
blogs.description: A lay‑person friendly deep dive into the core idea of the paper—how preserving the pairwise angles between neurons (hyperspherical energy) keeps the semantic power of large text‑to‑image diffusion models intact. The post uses visual analogies like phase vs. magnitude in Fourier transforms and simple toy experiments to explain why orthogonal transformations are the sweet spot for stable finetuning.

blogs.title: From DreamBooth to OFT: Making Personalized Image Generation Faster and More Reliable
blogs.description: Explains how Orthogonal Finetuning (and its constrained variant COFT) improve subject‑driven generation compared to classic DreamBooth and LoRA. The blog walks through training stability, convergence speed, and quantitative metrics (DINO, CLIP‑I, LPIPS) while keeping the technical jargon accessible to creative technologists.

blogs.title: Controlling Images with a Light Touch: How OFT Outperforms ControlNet and T2I‑Adapter
blogs.description: Shows how orthogonal finetuning adds precise control signals (edges, segmentation maps, facial landmarks) without extra inference overhead. Highlights the new control‑consistency metric introduced in the paper and presents intuitive examples from Canny‑to‑image, segmentation‑to‑image, and landmark‑to‑face tasks.

blogs.title: Orthogonal Finetuning vs. LoRA: Two Paths to Parameter‑Efficient Model Adaptation
blogs.description: Compares the two popular parameter‑efficient finetuning strategies—LoRA’s low‑rank additive updates and OFT’s layer‑shared orthogonal rotations. The post uses clear diagrams and simple math to illustrate why OFT preserves hyperspherical energy while still being lightweight, and when each method might be preferable.

blogs.title: Future Directions: Scaling Orthogonal Finetuning and Compositional Control
blogs.description: A forward‑looking piece that discusses the open challenges highlighted by the authors—speeding up Cayley transforms, combining multiple OFT adapters for compositional tasks, and improving block‑diagonal efficiency. It translates these research questions into ideas that developers and hobbyists can experiment with today.
